examples.ko: 마트 계산대의 바코드 판독기가 고장 났어요.
examples.en: The barcode reader at the supermarket checkout is broken.
Please tap your card on the card reader.

examples.ko: 이 판독기는 지문도 읽을 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can this reader read fingerprints too?

examples.ko: 새 판독기를 사서 사무실 입구에 설치했어요.
examples.en: We bought a new reader and installed it at the office entrance.

examples.ko: 글자를 잘못 읽는 판독기 때문에 다시 해야 했어요.
examples.en: I had to do it again because of a reader that misread the characters.
At the library, they check book numbers with a reader.

explain: 바코드, 카드, 지문처럼 기계로 정보를 읽어 내는 장치에 써요. 일상에서는 '리더기'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for devices that read information by machine, such as barcodes, cards and fingerprints. In daily talk people also often say '리더기'.

examples.ko: 심장 판막에 문제가 있다고 의사가 말했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said there is a problem with my heart valve.

examples.ko: 판막 수술을 받고 건강이 많이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After the valve surgery, my health got much better.

examples.ko: 혈액이 거꾸로 흐르지 않도록 판막이 막아 줘요.
examples.en: The valve stops blood from flowing backward.
My grandfather had his heart valve replaced.
I learned that veins also have small valves.

examples.ko: 판막이 제대로 닫히지 않으면 숨이 차요.
examples.en: If the valve doesn't close properly, you get short of breath.

explain: 병원이나 건강 뉴스에서 '심장 판막'으로 자주 나와요. 수도나 가스 같은 기계 장치는 '밸브'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: It often appears in hospital and health news as 'heart valve'. Mechanical devices such as water or gas valves are called '밸브', so the two are kept apart.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 전국에 판매망을 갖추고 있어요.
examples.en: This company has a sales network across the country.

examples.ko: 판매망이 넓어서 어디서나 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: The sales network is wide, so you can buy it anywhere.
Sales went up after we expanded our online sales network.

examples.ko: 새 제품의 판매망을 해외로 넓힐 계획이에요.
examples.en: We plan to extend the new product's sales network overseas.
Products left out of the sales network are hard to find.
I'm worried because the sales network through agencies has collapsed.

explain: 물건을 파는 가게, 대리점, 온라인이 연결된 체계를 말할 때 써요. '판매망을 넓히다/확대하다/구축하다'처럼 자주 함께 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the connected system of shops, agencies and online channels that sell goods. It is often used in '판매망을 넓히다/확대하다/구축하다'.

examples.en: I sold my car to a used car dealer.

examples.ko: 판매업자는 손님에게 가격을 정확히 알려 줘야 해요.
examples.en: A seller has to tell customers the price accurately.

examples.ko: 이 상품은 등록된 판매업자만 팔 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only registered dealers can sell this product.

examples.ko: 시장에서 만난 판매업자가 값을 깎아 줬어요.
examples.en: The seller I met at the market gave me a discount.
I reported the seller who sold defective goods.
First check whether it is an official dealer.

explain: '판매자'는 파는 사람을 넓게 말하고, '판매업자'는 장사를 직업이나 사업으로 하는 사람이라는 느낌이 강해요. 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '사장님'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '판매자' means anyone who sells, while '판매업자' feels more like someone who sells as a job or business. It is common in news and legal talk, and in daily life people may say '사장님'.

examples.en: The state of the election flipped on the last day.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 경기 판세를 읽기가 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to read how the match between the two teams is going.

examples.ko: 바둑 해설자가 판세를 차분하게 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The Go commentator calmly explained how the game stood.
Right now the situation favors our side.

examples.ko: 여론조사만으로는 판세를 아직 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't know how things stand yet from polls alone.
When the tide turned against him, he went quiet.

explain: '상황'보다 선거, 경기, 바둑처럼 승부가 걸린 자리의 형세를 말할 때 써요. '판세가 기울다/뒤집히다/읽다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '상황', it is used for how things stand in a contest such as an election, match or Go game. It goes with '판세가 기울다/뒤집히다/읽다'.

examples.en: I heard he lived in a shanty town as a child.

examples.ko: 판자촌 집들은 지붕과 벽이 낡은 판자로 되어 있었어요.
examples.en: The houses in the shanty town had roofs and walls made of old boards.
Shanties stood packed tightly on the hillside.
That shanty town disappeared because of redevelopment.

examples.ko: 영화 속 판자촌 풍경이 너무 쓸쓸했어요.
examples.en: The shanty town scenery in the movie was so lonely.
I attend a group that helps people in the shanty town.

explain: 판자로 대충 지은 허름한 집들이 모인 동네예요. 산 위쪽의 가난한 동네를 말하는 '달동네'와 겹칠 때가 많지만, 판자촌은 집의 모양에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a neighborhood of shabby houses roughly built from boards. It often overlaps with '달동네' (a poor hillside neighborhood), but 판자촌 focuses on how the houses are built.

examples.ko: 그 복서는 열두 라운드 끝에 판정승을 거뒀어요.
examples.en: The boxer won by decision after twelve rounds.
It was a decision win, not a KO, so it was a bit disappointing.
He became champion with a decision win.
Even though he dominated the match, it ended as only a decision win.

examples.ko: 판정승 소식에 온 가족이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The whole family applauded at the news of the decision win.
The crowd cheered when the decision win was announced.

explain: KO나 TKO처럼 끝내지 못하고 심판 점수로 이길 때 써요. 반대말은 '판정패'이고, 복싱이나 격투기 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when a fight is not finished by KO or TKO and the win comes from the judges' scores. The opposite is '판정패', and it often appears in boxing and fighting news.

examples.ko: 우리 선수가 점수 차로 판정패를 당했어요.
examples.en: Our fighter lost by decision on points.
It was a loss by decision, so the result was disappointing.
Even after the decision loss, he smiled and shook hands.

examples.ko: 그는 판정패를 인정하고 다시 연습을 시작했어요.
examples.en: He accepted the decision loss and started training again.

examples.ko: 두 번 연속 판정패로 순위가 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: His ranking dropped after two decision losses in a row.
He lost by decision, but he fought well to the end.

explain: KO패와 달리 끝까지 싸운 뒤 심판 점수에서 지는 경우예요. 반대말은 '판정승'이고, 보통 '판정패를 당하다/하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike a KO loss, it means fighting to the end and then losing on the judges' scores. The opposite is '판정승', and people usually say '판정패를 당하다/하다'.

examples.en: These days fake news runs rampant on the internet.
I hate a world where lies run rampant.
They say thieves were everywhere in the old days.
Illegal ads are everywhere in every alley.

examples.ko: 거리에 쓰레기가 판치지 않게 같이 치워요.
examples.en: Let's clean up together so trash doesn't take over the street.
If rip-off prices run rampant, tourists decrease.

explain: 주로 좋지 않은 것이 마구 퍼져서 세력을 떨칠 때 써요. 좋은 일에는 잘 안 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '활개 치다'가 있어요. '판쳐요/판치는'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when something bad spreads widely and takes over, so it does not fit good things. A similar expression is '활개 치다'. Conjugations are '판쳐요' and '판치는'.

examples.ko: 팔도 사투리를 다 흉내 내는 개그맨이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a comedian who imitates dialects from all over Korea.
This song is famous all over the country.
I traveled around looking for good restaurants across the country.
People from all over the country gathered in one place.
I went around the whole country tasting traditional food.

examples.ko: 우리나라 팔도 중에 가 본 곳이 몇 군데예요?
examples.en: How many places in Korea have you been to?

explain: '전국'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 좀 더 예스럽고 정겨운 느낌이에요. '팔도 사투리', '팔도 음식'처럼 굳은 짝으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means the same as '전국' (the whole country) but feels older and warmer. It often appears in fixed pairs such as '팔도 사투리' and '팔도 음식'.

examples.en: The fish I caught flipped up with a jump.
The frog hopped and disappeared into the grass.
The startled child sprang up and sat.
The fish are flopping around inside the net.

examples.ko: 메뚜기가 내 손 위에서 팔딱 튀었어요.
examples.en: A grasshopper jumped up off my hand.
When the alarm rang this morning, I jumped out of bed.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 힘 있게 한 번 뛰는 모양이에요. 여러 번 뛰면 '팔딱팔딱'이라고 하고, 더 크고 무거운 느낌은 '펄떡'이에요.
explain_en: It describes something small and light making one lively jump. Repeated jumping is '팔딱팔딱', and '펄떡' gives a bigger, heavier feel.

examples.en: The caught fish is flopping on the floor.

examples.ko: 새우가 접시 위에서 팔딱거려서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The shrimp jumped around on the plate, and I was startled.
A frog is hopping around by the pond.

examples.ko: 방에서 팔딱거리지 말고 얌전히 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Don't jump around in the room; sit quietly.
The children were surprised to see the flopping fish.
The shrimp that had been jumping around went quiet before long.

explain: 살아 있는 작은 것이 계속 힘 있게 뛰는 모습에 써요. 물고기, 새우, 개구리 이야기에서 자주 나오고, '팔딱팔딱 뛰다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a small living thing continuing to jump energetically. It often comes up with fish, shrimp and frogs, and people also say '팔딱팔딱 뛰다'.

examples.ko: 아이가 바람에 도는 팔랑개비를 보며 웃어요.
examples.en: The child laughs watching the pinwheel spin in the wind.
A pinwheel spins only when the wind blows.
I bought a colorful pinwheel at the market.
He ran off swinging his arms like a pinwheel.

examples.ko: 창가에 매단 팔랑개비가 쉬지 않고 돌아요.
examples.en: The pinwheel hung by the window keeps spinning.

examples.ko: 팔랑개비에 바람을 불어 주니까 빙글빙글 돌았어요.
examples.en: When I blew on the pinwheel, it spun round and round.

explain: '바람개비'와 같은 장난감을 가리키고, 일상에서는 '바람개비'도 많이 써요. 팔이나 물건이 빠르게 빙글빙글 도는 모습을 '팔랑개비처럼'이라고 비유해요.
explain_en: It names the same toy as '바람개비', which is also widely used in daily life. '팔랑개비처럼' is used figuratively for arms or objects spinning fast.

examples.ko: 마당에 널어 둔 빨래가 바람에 팔랑거려요.
examples.en: The laundry hung in the yard flutters in the wind.
A butterfly flutters over the flowers.
The hem of my skirt flaps, so it's not comfortable to walk.
I can hear the window curtain fluttering.
A leaf fluttered and then fell onto the water.
The ribbon on her shoulder fluttered.

explain: 얇고 가벼운 것이 바람에 가볍게 흔들리는 모습에 써요. 크고 센 깃발은 '펄럭이다'가 더 자연스럽고, 보통 '팔랑팔랑'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes something thin and light moving gently in the wind. For big, strong flags '펄럭이다' sounds more natural, and '팔랑팔랑' is also common.

examples.ko: 아이들이 개울에 돌 팔매질을 하며 놀았어요.
examples.en: The children played by throwing stones into the stream.

examples.ko: 팔매질로 돌을 멀리 던지는 시합을 했어요.
examples.en: We had a contest to see who could throw a stone farthest.

examples.ko: 옛 이야기에는 팔매질로 새를 맞히는 소년이 나와요.
examples.en: An old tale features a boy who hits birds by throwing stones.
If you throw stones into the pond, the fish get scared.

examples.ko: 누가 창문에 팔매질을 해서 유리가 깨졌어요.
examples.en: Someone threw something at the window and the glass broke.

examples.ko: 팔매질이 서툴러서 돌이 바로 앞에 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: I'm bad at throwing, so the stone dropped right in front of me.

explain: 작은 돌 같은 것을 팔을 휘둘러 멀리 던지는 일이에요. 보통 '돌팔매질'로 많이 쓰고, 사람을 향해 하면 위험한 행동이에요.

phrases.example: 실수 한 번으로 온라인에서 돌팔매를 맞았어요.
phrases.en: Because of one mistake, I got savaged online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 돌을 맞는 게 아니라 여러 사람에게 심하게 비난받는다는 뜻으로 써요. 인터넷이나 뉴스 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean being hit by real stones but being harshly criticized by many people. You often hear it in talk about the internet and the news.

explain_en: It means swinging your arm to throw something small like a stone far. People mostly say '돌팔매질', and doing it toward a person is dangerous.

en: person who brags about their own family

examples.ko: 자기 아이 자랑만 하니 팔불출이 따로 없네요.
examples.en: He only brags about his kid; he's a textbook doting parent.

examples.ko: 남편 자랑을 했더니 친구가 팔불출이라고 놀렸어요.
examples.en: When I bragged about my husband, my friend teased me for being a show-off.
I admit I'm a bit of a proud bragger about my own.

examples.ko: 팔불출 소리를 들어도 딸 사진은 보여 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: Even if you call me a show-off, I want to show you my daughter's photos.

examples.ko: 아내 칭찬을 하루 종일 하는 그는 팔불출이에요.
examples.en: He praises his wife all day long; he's a real brag.
I held back my bragging so I wouldn't look like a show-off.

explain: 자기 가족이나 자기 것을 지나치게 자랑하는 사람을 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요. 친한 사이에서 농담으로 쓰고, 스스로 '저 팔불출이죠?'라고 웃으며 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It teasingly names someone who brags too much about their own family or belongings. It is used jokingly between close people, and speakers sometimes laugh and say it about themselves.

en: duck-footed walk; walking with toes turned out

examples.en: My grandfather walks slowly with his toes pointed out.

examples.ko: 저는 팔자걸음이라서 운동화가 금방 닳는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I walk with my feet turned out, so my sneakers seem to wear out fast.
I practice walking to fix my turned-out gait.
His walk is so splayed that I recognized him from far away.
Walking with my toes out has been a habit since I was little.
The child waddling duck-like with toes out is cute.

explain: 발끝을 바깥쪽으로 벌리고 걷는 걸음이에요. 반대로 발끝이 안쪽으로 모이는 걸음은 '안짱걸음'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a way of walking with the toes turned outward. The opposite, with the toes pointing inward, is called '안짱걸음'.

en: with a jump; with a hop

examples.en: The frog hopped into the pond.

examples.ko: 시험에 합격했다는 말에 팔짝 뛰며 좋아했어요.
examples.en: I jumped for joy when I heard I passed the exam.
The cat leaped up onto the wall.
The puppy keeps jumping up and down when it sees me.

examples.ko: 문이 열리자 아이들이 팔짝 하고 튀어나왔어요.
examples.en: When the door opened, the children sprang out.
I was so startled that I almost jumped.

explain: 가볍고 빠르게 한 번 뛰는 모양이에요. 기뻐서 뛸 때도, 놀라서 뛸 때도 쓰고, 반복하면 '팔짝팔짝'이 돼요.

phrases.example: 이렇게 억울한 일은 처음이라 팔짝 뛰겠어요.
phrases.en: I've never been so wronged; I could hit the roof.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁘거나 화가 나서 가만히 있지 못할 정도일 때 써요. 특히 억울하거나 화날 때 '팔짝 뛰겠다'라고 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so happy or angry that you can't stay still. It is most often said about anger or a sense of injustice.

explain_en: It describes a light, quick single jump. It is used for jumping from joy or from surprise, and repeating it gives '팔짝팔짝'.

examples.en: The water in the pot is boiling hard.

examples.ko: 국이 팔팔 끓으면 불을 줄여 주세요.
examples.en: When the soup is boiling hard, please turn down the heat.
Put the noodles into the boiling water.
Even though she is old, my grandmother is full of energy.
Now that my cold is gone, I feel full of energy.
The fish at the fish market still look fresh and lively.

explain: 물이 세게 끓는 모양을 나타내고, '팔팔 끓다'로 자주 써요. 더 크고 세게 끓으면 '펄펄'이라고 하며, '팔팔하다'는 기운이 넘치고 싱싱하다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It shows water boiling vigorously and is often used as '팔팔 끓다'. A bigger, stronger boil is '펄펄', and '팔팔하다' is also used for being full of energy or fresh.

examples.en: A fanfare rang out loudly at the opening ceremony.
The awards ceremony began with a fanfare.
The players entered as a fanfare sounded.
The children were startled by the sound of the fanfare.
They announced it quietly, without a big fanfare.
A fanfare echoed at the news of the victory.

explain: 행사나 의식을 시작할 때 나팔로 크게 연주하는 음악을 말해요. 표준 표기는 '팡파르'이고, '팡파레'는 흔한 잘못된 표기예요.
explain_en: It is the loud trumpet music played to start an event or ceremony. The standard spelling is '팡파르', and '팡파레' is a common misspelling.

examples.en: I coated the injeolmi generously with red bean powder.
The red bean topping is sweet, so I keep eating.
My grandmother steamed red bean sirutteok for me.
I boiled the beans for a long time to make red bean topping.

examples.ko: 이 떡은 팥고물 때문에 손에 많이 묻어요.
examples.en: This rice cake gets all over my hands because of the red bean topping.

examples.ko: 팥고물 대신 콩고물을 묻힌 떡도 맛있어요.
examples.en: Rice cakes coated with soybean powder instead of red bean are tasty too.

explain: 떡 겉에 묻히거나 켜켜이 넣는 팥 가루예요. 찐빵처럼 안에 넣는 팥은 '팥소'라고 해서 구분하고, 콩으로 만든 것은 '콩고물'이에요.
explain_en: It is the red bean powder coated on rice cakes or layered between them. Bean paste put inside, as in steamed buns, is called '팥소', and the soybean version is '콩고물'.

en: ruining both oneself and one's family

examples.ko: 사업에 실패해 패가망신한 사람 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about a man who lost everything after his business failed.

examples.ko: 투자 사기를 당하면 패가망신할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you fall for an investment scam, you could be utterly ruined.
He was completely ruined because of a huge debt.
If you take on more debt, it's easy to be ruined.

examples.ko: 어머니는 보증을 서면 패가망신한다고 늘 말씀하세요.
examples.en: My mother always says that if you cosign a loan you'll be ruined.
Be careful not to step onto the path of total ruin.

explain: 집안의 재산을 잃고 명예까지 잃어 완전히 망한다는 강한 말이에요. 주로 빚, 보증, 사기 같은 일을 경고할 때 '패가망신하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is a strong word for losing family fortune and reputation and being totally ruined. It is mostly used as '패가망신하다' when warning about debt, cosigning loans or fraud.

en: being full of go; vigorous; ebullient

examples.en: The new employee greeted everyone full of spirit.
Spirited young men founded a new company.
That player is young, but his eyes are full of fight.
I like that confident, driven look on your face.
I was full of drive at first, but reality wasn't easy.
The junior who used to be so spirited has gone quiet lately.

explain: 젊은 사람이 용기와 의욕이 넘칠 때 칭찬하듯 쓰는 말이에요. '패기 있다'라고도 말하고, 보통 나이 많은 사람에게는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is a mostly complimentary word for a young person bursting with courage and drive. You can also say '패기 있다', and it is not usually used for older people.

examples.en: That story sounds like a paradox.

examples.ko: 일을 줄일수록 일이 늘어나는 건 패러독스예요.
examples.en: It's a paradox that the more you cut work, the more work grows.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 시간 여행의 패러독스를 다뤄요.
examples.en: This movie deals with the paradox of time travel.
We discussed paradoxes in class.
They say this paradox has not been solved yet.
His words, full of paradoxes, were interesting.

explain: '역설'과 같은 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '모순'이나 '아이러니'라고도 하지만, 패러독스는 맞는 말 같은데 결론이 이상한 경우에 주로 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '역설'. In daily talk people also say '모순' or '아이러니', but 패러독스 is mostly for cases that seem logical yet lead to a strange conclusion.

examples.ko: 부모를 버리는 일은 패륜이라는 비판을 받아요.
examples.en: Abandoning one's parents is criticized as an immoral act.

examples.ko: 어른께 막말하는 건 패륜에 가까운 행동이에요.
examples.en: Speaking rudely to an elder comes close to a breach of moral duty.

examples.ko: 그 드라마는 패륜을 다뤄서 논란이 됐어요.
examples.en: That drama stirred controversy by dealing with immoral conduct.

examples.ko: 패륜적인 말에 사람들이 크게 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: People were very angry at the immoral remarks.

examples.ko: 패륜이라는 단어는 쉽게 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't use the word immoral so lightly.

examples.ko: 가족 사이의 패륜을 다룬 소설을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a novel about immoral conduct within a family.

explain: 부모나 윗사람에게 사람으로서 지켜야 할 도리를 어기는 일을 가리켜요. 뉴스나 드라마에서 강하게 비난할 때 쓰는 무거운 말이라 사람에게 함부로 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It refers to breaking the basic duty one owes to parents and elders. It is a heavy word used for strong condemnation in news and dramas, so people avoid applying it carelessly to someone.

examples.en: A sense of defeat washed over me after I failed the exam.

examples.ko: 패배감에 빠지지 말고 다시 도전해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't sink into a sense of defeat; try again.
As I kept losing, only the feeling of defeat grew.
He exercised every day to overcome his feeling of defeat.
A sense of defeat shows on your face even if you don't say it.

examples.ko: 졌다는 패배감 때문에 밥도 먹기 싫었어요.
examples.en: I didn't even want to eat because of the sense of having lost.

explain: '졌다'는 느낌 자체를 말해요. 남보다 못하다는 느낌인 '열등감'과 달리, 겨루거나 시도해서 졌을 때의 기분이에요. '패배감에 빠지다/젖다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of having lost. Unlike '열등감' (a sense of being inferior to others), it is the mood after losing a contest or an attempt. It is used as '패배감에 빠지다/젖다'.

examples.ko: 패배주의에 빠지면 시작도 하기 전에 포기해요.
examples.en: If you fall into defeatism, you give up before even starting.
He decided to drop his defeatist thinking.
The coach worried about the players' defeatism.
If defeatism spreads, the team atmosphere gets worse.
The thought that it won't work anyway is defeatism.

examples.ko: 패배주의는 노력도 하기 전에 포기하게 만들어요.
examples.en: Defeatism makes you give up before you even try.

explain: 해 보기 전부터 '어차피 질 거야'라고 생각하는 태도예요. 반대로 잘될 거라고 보는 태도는 '낙관주의'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the attitude of thinking 'we'll lose anyway' before even trying. The opposite attitude of expecting things to turn out well is called '낙관주의'.
